EO 6859, EO 6513-J, EO 6678-A held texts checked
reasoning: Judgment call tested on the merits: a general clause order. The lead command orders that the expense-collection clause 'or any appropriate modification thereof shall become effective as a part of any code of fair competition approved under said Title.' The clause takes effect on application through a code's amendment procedure or by representative associations, and only if the Administrator finds it necessary. In substance the order authorizes in advance an amendment to approved codes, so the authority it exercises is the section 3 power to approve codes and amendments. Every provision of the clause operates only inside an approved code: section 1 and its paragraphs (a) to (c), on the Code Authority's obligations, budget and contributions, including suits in its own name, and section 2, on who may help select the Code Authority and who may use the NRA emblem. S.J. Res. 113 section 2 repealed both the power to approve codes and every provision for enforcing them. The lead command therefore had nothing to attach to after June 14, 1935, and each incorporated clause ended with its code. The six-row inventory is complete. My searches found no held order citing EO 6678 by number. The 'No. 6678' hits are a public land order and FR page numbers, and EO 6678-A is a different order extending the President's Reemployment Agreement. No held order revokes or modifies EO 6678. EO 6513-J's inter-code contribution arrangement is separate. EO 6859 (September 27, 1934) transferred the Administrator's powers to the National Industrial Recovery Board. That transfer changed who made the finding the lead command requires, so it is a later event under the shared analysis's treatment of administrative orders; it is not an end, and the claim's omission of it does not affect the end. Contributions owed and suits begun before the repeal are accrued, as the savings check says. One minor point: the earlier_end_check repeats template wording about 'this code or this approval', which does not fit an order that names no code. It is not material. First end: 1935-06-14 by S.J. Res. 113 section 2.

reasoning: Judgment call tested on the merits: the registration condition. The operative text approves the Trucking Industry code 'with the following condition': vehicles of enterprises principally warehousing furniture and household goods that fall within Article II, section 1, subsection A, paragraph (1) of the code 'shall be registered, in such form and manner and within such period as the Administrator may determine, with the Code Committee' for the proposed Household Goods Storage and Moving code, 'and, if such a Code is approved, then, thereafter with the Code Authority established under said Code.' The condition is imposed under section 3(a), which allows the President to attach conditions to an approval. It binds only vehicles covered by the Trucking code, and its word 'thereafter' moves the registration duty to the new Code Authority once that code is approved. That code was approved by EO 6684-D on April 19, 1934. So the condition sets a continuing registration status for covered vehicles, including vehicles that came under the code later. It is not a one-time act exhausted by a single performance, and the claim is right to keep it with the approval. If one read the condition as a one-time registration, the held record would not show whether or when that registration took place, so under the owner's 2026-10-28 ruling that reading could not supply an earlier date either. The approval stayed in force at least until December 19, 1934: EO 6925 recites 'the Code of Fair Competition for the Trucking Industry approved February 10, 1934' as the code that would govern most of the Cinders trade's transport operations. EO 6684-D, which I read, provided for a hearing on whether used-household-goods vehicles belong under the Trucking code; the result is not held, and the claim says so. Any reassignment would have narrowed the coverage the condition reaches, an amendment-type later event; it would not have cancelled this approval. First end: 1935-06-14 by S.J. Res. 113 section 2. Identity checks pass (the WPA list reads 'conditionally approved'). Searches are adequate; the only 'No. 6600' hit is a public land order. Drafting correction, not material to the verdict: the earlier_end_check carries the template sentence 'the order states no period, condition or until date of its own'. Read literally, that sentence is false for an order approved with a condition containing an Administrator-set period. It should say that the order states no period, condition or date that ends the approval. The rest of the claim analyses the condition correctly, so the end, mechanism and reasons are unaffected.
